name: Wyze Plug Outdoor

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (no 5 GHz). Bluetooth 4.2 is used during setup.

matter.note: Wyze's pages for this plug name Alexa and Google Assistant only and don't mention Matter. That's an absence, not an explicit no.

apple_home.note: Wyze's integration list (Alexa, Google Assistant, IFTTT) leaves out HomeKit, but we found no Wyze page saying the outdoor plug is unsupported.

google_home.note: Link your Wyze account in the Google Home app. Wyze's Google Assistant device list names the Plug Outdoor, and Wyze says the integration is supported in the US only.

smartthings.note: SmartThings isn't on Wyze's integration list, but Wyze doesn't say it's unsupported.

home_assistant.note: No official Wyze integration in Home Assistant; only community custom integrations that use the Wyze cloud.

hubRequired.note: Wyze's product page lists Hub Required: No. It joins 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi directly and is set up in the Wyze app.

localControl.note: Wyze says the light sensor keeps switching the plug without Wi-Fi once configured, but we found no statement on local network control without the Wyze cloud.

energyMonitoring.note: Usage history in the Wyze app, with alerts when monthly use passes a set level.

maxLoadWatts.note: Wyze gives 15 A max per outlet (120 V, 60 Hz) with overload protection and a 1/2 HP motor limit, but no wattage figure.

summary: Only two assistants are confirmed for the Wyze Plug Outdoor (WLPPO1): Alexa through the Wyze skill, and Google Home through a Wyze account link that Wyze supports in the US only. Apple Home and SmartThings aren't on Wyze's integration list, and Wyze doesn't mention Matter. It joins 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi directly, uses Bluetooth for setup, and logs energy use in the Wyze app with alerts when a month's use passes your limit. Once set up, its light sensor keeps switching the plug even if Wi-Fi drops.
caveats: Wyze says its Google Assistant integration is officially supported in the US only.
Apple Home and SmartThings aren't on Wyze's integration list.
Rated 15 A per outlet; Wyze doesn't publish a wattage limit.
No official Home Assistant integration, only community ones that use the Wyze cloud.
